Green chile cheese dip, warm corn chips.How to make it1 tbsp butter1/2 brown onion, finely diced1 garlic clove, crushed200g jar roasted green chiles, chopped1 tbsp cornflour250ml evaporated milk200g tasty cheese, grated100g Monterey Jack or mozzarella, grated1 tsp ground cumin230g bag corn chipsSoften the onion and garlic in the butter.Toss the cheeses with the cornflour.Add the evaporated milk and cumin to the pan, bring to a simmer, then stir in the cheese a handful at a time until smooth.Stir through the green chiles, season and serve hot with the chips, warmed in the oven.Split-in-two loaded potato skinsOne embryo split in two. Crisp skins, cheddar, sour cream, jalapeño.How to make it6 medium potatoes2 tbsp olive oil150g cheddar, grated150g sour cream3 spring onions, sliced2 tbsp pickled jalapeños, chopped1 tsp smoked paprikaBake the potatoes at 200°C until soft, then cool a little.Halve them and scoop out most of the flesh, leaving a thin wall. Keep the flesh for another day.Brush inside and out with oil, season with salt and paprika and bake until crisp.Fill with cheddar and bake until bubbling, then top with sour cream, spring onion and jalapeños.Island fruit saladJulius grew up on an island. Vincent didn't.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.Blue PlatesGreen chile cheeseburgersJulius tells Traven he'll be back. Roasted green chile, cheddar, griddled onions.How to make it600g beef mince, 20 per cent fat1 brown onion, thinly sliced1 tbsp butter150g jar roasted green chiles, chopped4 slices of cheddar4 soft burger buns4 iceberg lettuce leaves1 tomato, sliced3 tbsp whole-egg mayonnaiseCook the onion slowly in the butter until soft and golden, then push to the side of the griddle.Shape the mince into 4 thin patties and season hard.Griddle on high for 3 minutes, flip, pile on the green chile and cheese and cook until melted.Toast the buns, spread with mayo and build with lettuce, tomato, patty and onions.Thanksgiving hot turkey plateVincent asks about Thanksgiving dinner. Turkey on toast, mash, gravy, cranberry.How to make it600g roast turkey breast, sliced1kg floury potatoes, peeled80g butter125ml milk2 tbsp plain flour500ml chicken stock1 tsp thyme leaves4 thick slices of white bread150g cranberry sauce200g frozen peasBoil the potatoes until soft, then mash with 50g butter and the hot milk.Cook the rest of the butter with the flour, whisk in the stock and thyme and simmer to a gravy.Warm the turkey slices gently in the gravy.Cook the peas and toast the bread.Lay turkey on the toast, smother with gravy and serve with mash, peas and cranberry.The Pie CaseSix-father sopaipillasWe had six fathers, says Julius. Puffed fried pastry, honey butter, cinnamon.How to make it250g plain flour2 tsp baking powder1/2 tsp salt1 tbsp butter, plus 60g softened180ml warm water1 L vegetable oil, for frying4 tbsp honey2 tbsp caster sugar1 tsp ground cinnamonRub 1 tbsp butter into the flour, baking powder and salt, then mix in the water to a soft dough and rest 10 minutes.Roll out 5mm thick and cut into 12 squares.Fry a few at a time at 190°C, spooning oil over until they puff, then flip and drain.Whip the softened butter with the honey, toss the sopaipillas in cinnamon sugar and serve with the honey butter.The FountainWhere they made the milkshakeVincent finds where they made the milkshake. Thick vanilla malt shake, whipped cream.How to make it8 big scoops of vanilla ice cream400ml cold milk4 tbsp malted milk powder1 tsp vanilla extract150ml thickened cream, whipped4 maraschino cherriesBlend the ice cream, milk, malt powder and vanilla until thick and smooth.Pour into 4 frosted glasses.Top with whipped cream and a cherry and serve with long spoons and straws.Bottomless diner coffeePour it strong.
